title: Annotatio IV §.XIX close: Vladislaus confession — four Scripture heads; neither corporal nor bare sign — stop before §.XX
pass_a_gloss: Further in part 2… the Waldenses at p. 292 are said to propose four things divine Scripture would have us believe concerning the Eucharistic Sacrament: First, that this Sacrament is bread and wine. Second, that that bread is Christ’s true body and the wine Christ’s true Blood… But if anyone would first thrust an intellect on Christ’s words in a preposterous order… so that either he lifts himself too high — wishing the whole Christ living there CORPORALLY or personally present to our bodies… or on the contrary casts himself too low… so that he bears Christ to be here by no means, but only a BARE and bloodless Sign doing nothing in the soul… Third… the New Testament… Fourth… that bread is participation of Christ’s body and the Wine of His Blood… inculcating countless times the Spiritual mode of eating Christ’s Body, the corporal shut out…
pass_b_english: Waldenses to Vladislaus (part 2): Scripture proposes four heads — (1) the Sacrament is bread and wine; (2) that bread/wine are Christ’s true body and Blood; (3) New Testament/covenant; (4) participation of body and blood.

Beware two ditches: lifting too high into CORPORAL/personal presence to our bodies, or sinking to a BARE bloodless Sign — they inculcate Spiritual eating, corporal shut out. Stop before §.XX (Lutheran comparison).
source_text: Præterea parte 2. … Waldenses pag. 292. de Sacramento Eucharistiæ quatuor nobis divinam Scripturam credenda proponere perhibent, quorum Primum faciunt, quod Sacramentum hoc, panis & vinum sit. Secundum, quod panis ille sit verum corpus Christi, & vinum sit verus Sanguis Christi… Quibus quidem verbis Christi si quis præpostero ordine priùs velit intellectum obtrudere… ut aut nimis in altum se subvehat, hoc est, quod velit integrum Christum inibi viventem CORPORALITER seu personaliter præsentem corporibus nostris… aut è diverso minus sese in ima dejiciat … ut nullo modo Christum hic esse ferat, sed solum NUDUM & exsangue ac nihil operans in anima, SIGNUM… Tertium… Novum Testamentum… Quartum… panis ille sit participatio corporis Christi & Vinum Sanguinis ejus… Spiritualem manducandi Corporis Christi modum, excluso corporali, innumeris vicibus inculcantes…
notes: Four heads; neither corporal nor bare sign; stop §.XX.
